ops.title: Spawn costs ~26ms dominated by durable fsync, not exec — the csops gate is free
ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-01 by the P4.1 Lane C refuter on Apple M5 Max / macOS 26, correcting a design
estimate that was wrong by more than an order of magnitude.

    BenchmarkProcessTokenSelf-18          3017 ns/op   # token mint alone
    BenchmarkVerifyProcessSelf-18         5145 ns/op   # full VerifyProcess, denial path
    BenchmarkStoreSpawnNoGate-18      27084696 ns/op   # Store.Spawn -> exit, Verify nil
    BenchmarkStoreSpawnFullVerifyGate 26180235 ns/op   # same, gate runs full VerifyProcess

Two conclusions:

1. **The Cmd.Exec csops gate is free.** It is indistinguishable from noise — well under 1% of a
   spawn, not the ~6% the F1b spike estimated. There is no cost argument against verifying every
   spawned child's code identity.

2. **A spawn costs ~26ms, and exec is not where it goes.** The design's "~1.6ms posix_spawn"
   understates the real per-spawn cost by roughly 17x. The time is the durable record fsync plus the
   retire fsync — daemonkit records a child before its first instruction and again when it retires,
   and those two fsyncs dominate.

That second point matters for any consumer thinking about spawn-heavy work: the record is the cost,
not the process. A consumer running N short commands pays 2N fsyncs. Ctx.Run is not a cheap
primitive, and nothing in the API says so.

Related: [[csops-audittoken-reads-a-suspended-child]] for the feasibility measurement this refines.
